newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to resume arms sales to Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to resume arms sales to Rwanda.

text.p: South Africa said on Wednesday it was lifting a ban on arms sales to Rwanda after assurances that no weapons would be used abroad.

Pretoria suspended a deal worth 87 million rand ($19 million) in November after reports that Rwandan troops were involved in the rebellion in next-door Zaire which eventually toppled president Mobutu Sese Seko.

Kader Asmal, a member of President Nelson Mandela's cabinet and chairman of the state arms control committee, told a news conference the decision was due to Rwanda's need to strengthen its capacity to defend its statehood.
"The non-lethal and non-sensitive material which was previously ordered but stopped will now be allowed to be exported to Rwanda," he said.
"This follows specific assurances from the vice president of Rwanda (Paul Kagame) that the material will not be used outside Rwanda."
South African officials have refused to detail the types of arms offered for sale, describing them merely as "defensive".

Laurent Kabila's Tutsi-dominated rebellion in Zaire led to the repatriation of around a million Rwandan Hutus. They had fled to camps in Zaire in 1994 after Hutu extremists massacred several hundred thousand Tutsi countrymen in a genocide.
Since their return home, killings and political instability in now Tutsi-controlled Rwanda have increased.

Asmal said Kagame, a Tutsi who masterminded the defeat of the former Hutu regime and now also serves as defence minister, had assured him Rwanda would act against those who violated human rights and would respect the Geneva conventions on the conduct of war.
Aid workers have persistently alleged that Kabila's forces or his allies from Rwanda or Uganda massacred thousands of Hutu refugees during Zaire's seven-month civil war.
